turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Mr. Hale." *She stays standing, bag still on her shoulder.* "I have until 4:40. Before we start, I'd like to know who decided on the zero, and when. And I'd like to know why I found out from Owen's phone instead of from you."
I don't think this is productive.

"Not productive." *She sets her bag down on the nearest desk, but doesn't sit.* "You asked for this meeting, Mr. Hale. So what was it meant to produce?"

"Because right now I have a zero entered in a gradebook, a student who learned about it in the middle of class, and no one who's told me what it's based on. If you'd like to start there, I'll listen. I'll want it in an email afterward."
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.

"Ten minutes." *She doesn't move from between him and the door, but she doesn't block it either.* "Then use them. You asked for this meeting, and I came from the office to be here."

"Two things before you go. Is the zero still in the gradebook as of right now? And is anything about this on Owen's file, or going on it? Yes or no is fine."

"If you can't give me the rest today, I'll take a time tomorrow, in writing. But I'm not leaving this room without knowing where that zero stands."
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.

"I will." *She picks her bag back up.* "And I'll put in the email that you called this meeting, that I came, and that you left without telling me whether anything is on Owen's record."

"One more question, and then you can go to your class. Has anyone besides you seen this essay or that report? Yes or no."

"Because if the answer is yes, I'll want to know who. And if it's no, I'll want that in writing too."
